what: Rotate & Flip Image turns pictures the right way round. Rotate left or right by 90 degrees, turn upside down by 180, or set any angle to straighten a tilted horizon. Flip horizontally to mirror a selfie, or vertically to turn it upside down.
You can add many pictures at once: the same rotation is used for every one, and you download them in a ZIP. Pictures keep their own format (JPG stays JPG, PNG stays PNG) unless you choose another.
All the work happens in your browser, so your photos are never uploaded.
uses: Turn photos that show up on their side in emails, websites or slides.
Rotate a beach or city photo by a degree or two and crop the corners.
Flip a front-camera photo so writing reads the right way.
Rotate a batch of scans or document photos in one go.
Mirror icons, arrows and shapes for left and right versions.
Turn landscape pictures to portrait before printing.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop images here" and choose one or more files. With several pictures, thumbnails appear: tap one to preview it, or ✕ to remove it.
Press "Rotate left", "Rotate right" or "180°". Press again to keep turning.
Press "Flip horizontal" to mirror left and right, or "Flip vertical" to mirror top and bottom.
Move "Any angle" or type a number such as -3.5 in the box next to it.
Choose what happens to the corners
With a tilted angle, "Show whole image, fill corners" keeps everything and fills the corners using "Corner fill"; "Crop off the empty corners" cuts the largest clean rectangle.
"Save as" keeps the original format, or choose JPG, PNG or WebP and the quality.
Press "Download this image", or "Download all as ZIP" for every picture.
features: Quick buttons plus a fine slider and number box in 0.1° steps.
Mirror pictures in either direction, together with rotation.
One setting for many pictures, saved in a single ZIP.
Fill with transparency, white, black or any colour, or crop to the largest clean rectangle.
JPG, PNG and WebP stay as they were unless you choose otherwise.
Very large results are reduced to a size phones can save, and the tool tells you.

example.title: Worked example: twelve sideways photos
example.text: Marco copied 12 photos from an old camera and they all appear on their side. He drops all 12 onto the page, presses "Rotate right" once and checks a few thumbnails. "Save as" is "Same as original", so they stay JPGs at 92% quality. He presses "Download all 12 as ZIP" and gets rotated-images.zip with files like IMG_0412-rotated.jpg.

tips: For a tilted horizon, a small angle like 1 to 3 degrees is usually enough.
Choose PNG and Transparent corners if you will place the rotated picture on a coloured background.
All pictures in a batch get the same rotation, so batch pictures that need the same fix.
Use "Reset" to go back to the original without reopening the files.
Flip horizontal is the usual fix for mirrored text in selfies.
problems: The rotated picture has white corners
JPG cannot be see-through. Choose PNG or WebP, or pick "Crop off the empty corners".
The result is smaller than expected
Very large rotated results are reduced to about 16 megapixels so phones can save them. The message tells you when.
My iPhone photo will not open
HEIC photos cannot be read by most browsers. Convert them to JPG first with the HEIC to JPG tool.
Use the green Download button under the buttons. Some browsers block automatic downloads.
